action: Do not paste commands from websites into Run or PowerShell; check game availability through official publisher channels. If the command was run, disconnect the machine, scan it with trusted software and change passwords from a clean device, starting with email.
date_note: Date of the Bitdefender Labs post; the site's first activity is not stated
exec: A fake GTA VI download site installs a stealer that takes browser, wallet and account credentials from Windows PCs.
geo_basis: no victim or place stated; global lure
plain: A website offers a fake GTA VI client for PC and tells visitors to paste a command into Windows. Bitdefender says this installs a likely Rust-based information stealer. GTA VI is not available on PC.
summary: Bitdefender Labs describes a lure site offering a fake GTA VI PC streaming client, installed by a ZIP or by a ClickFix command pasted into Win+R that runs PowerShell. The chain side-loads a DLL and injects a payload Bitdefender calls likely a new or modified Rust-based stealer, taking browser credentials, wallet data and clipboard contents. The post names no actor.
title: Fake GTA VI PC client spreads stealer malware through a ClickFix attack, Bitdefender says

validation.note: Bitdefender Labs post read in full (vendor analysis); no second publisher read. The post says the PowerShell-fetched script itself is not included.
